subject.title: feat(apps,ui): question surface parity and composer takeover

question: Should OpenClaw standardize persistent question summaries, Skip, and panel-as-composer behavior as the cross-client interaction contract after the reused-ID repair is complete?
rationale: This PR changes long-lived interaction behavior across three native clients and the Control UI; code review can validate mechanics but cannot establish the intended permanent product contract.

options.title: Adopt the parity contract
options.body: Repair reused-ID lifecycle handling, require native runtime proof, and merge the unified persistent-summary and composer-takeover behavior.

options.title: Narrow the rollout
options.body: Keep the recovery and Skip fixes but defer the permanent summary or web composer-takeover policy to a smaller owner-approved change.

options.title: Pause for a product spec
options.body: Hold the branch until maintainers document which question states should persist and how each surface should present them.

recommendation.title: Adopt the parity contract
recommendation.body: Repair reused-ID lifecycle handling, require native runtime proof, and merge the unified persistent-summary and composer-takeover behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The branch and stated product direction are centered on the question-surface parity work they authored.
